h1: The 6 Best Mini PC Monitor Mounts of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Mini PC Monitor Mounts: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six mini PC monitor mounts for VESA backs and monitor arms, with weight ratings and width ranges compared.
summary: The Adjustable Thin Client bracket attached to a monitor arm is the best mini PC monitor mount, carrying 12 lb across a wide 0.63 to 2.8 inch fit range for under $25. HumanCentric is the choice for heavier monitors, VIVO leads on warranty, and a Dell-specific VIVO model suits OptiPlex Micro owners.
intro: Hanging a mini PC off the back of a monitor clears desk space, but it changes the load your arm carries. The VESA pattern on a display is rated for the display, and a thin arm may sit close to its limit before a computer is added. That is the number most shoppers forget to check.

Six mounts were ranked using the listed VESA patterns, device width range, weight capacity and ventilation. We weighed how safely and how widely each one fits, using the listings alone. Always add your monitor and PC weights together and compare them with the arm's own rating.

products.name: Adjustable Thin Client Mini PC Mount Bracket, Attached to Monitor Arm
products.verdict: A metal bracket that fits 0.63 to 2.8 inch devices and carries 12 lb.
products.description:
This metal bracket accepts devices 0.63 to 2.8 inches wide and carries 12 lb. It mounts to a monitor arm, a wall or under a desk, and comes with cable management and a pen holder. It costs under $25.

The combination of width range, capacity and price carries it to first place. Against HumanCentric, it holds more on its own, at 12 lb to 11 lb, although it publishes no combined rating with the monitor, so you must do that math yourself. Metal construction adds a little weight.

Buy it for a typical mini PC on a monitor arm. The caveat is load: check how much weight your arm has left after the display, because the listing gives you no combined figure to lean on.
products.idealFor: Most mini PCs on monitor arms.
products.skipIf: Your arm is near its limit.

products.name: HumanCentric Thin Client Mount Bracket, Mini PC to Monitor Arm
products.verdict: The only bracket here with a stated combined rating alongside the monitor.
products.description:
HumanCentric's bracket fits VESA 75x75 and 100x100mm, accepts devices 0.65 to 2.55 inches deep, and lists an 11 lb device rating with 18 lb combined alongside the monitor. Silicone scratch strips and wall and under-desk hardware are included. It sits in the $25 to $50 bucket.

A stated combined rating is rare, and it is the reason this model ranks second. It reassures anyone with a heavier monitor who worries about total load. The tradeoffs are a narrower depth range than the leader and a higher price bucket.

Choose it for heavier displays near their arm limit. Skip it if your PC is thicker than 2.55 inches, since the cheaper first-place bracket accepts more. Check your arm's own rating even then, because the combined figure applies to the bracket.

products.name: VIVO Adjustable Thin Client Mini PC Mount, Attached to Monitor
products.description:
VIVO's thin client mount is powder-coated solid steel with VESA 75x75 and 100x100mm support, a 1.8 to 7.1 cm width range and a 5 kg (about 11 lb) rating. It carries a 3-year warranty and falls in the under $25 bucket.

It takes third place because the 12 lb pick holds slightly more and fits a wider range. Against HumanCentric, it undercuts on price and adds a longer warranty, though it gives you no combined rating or scratch strips. It also lacks cable extras.

Buy it if backing matters and your PC fits within 7.1 cm. Skip it if you need the full 12 lb capacity. The warranty is the strongest reason to pick it, especially for a device you plan to leave mounted for years.

products.name: VIVO Behind Monitor Mini PC Mount for Dell OptiPlex Micro
products.verdict: A ventilated mount that conceals a Dell OptiPlex Micro behind the screen.
products.description:
This VIVO model is built for the Dell OptiPlex Micro. It fits VESA 75x75 and 100x100mm, attaches behind the screen out of sight, and uses a ventilated open structure. Desk and wall hardware are included, and it costs under $25.

For that one device family, a dedicated mount holds the machine more rigidly than a universal clamp and keeps it hidden. It ranks fourth because it fits nothing else, and the listing states no weight rating. Compared with the universal brackets above, flexibility is the cost.

Buy it if you own an OptiPlex Micro and want a clean behind-monitor look. Skip it for any other brand. The ventilated frame helps with heat, but leave breathing room around the vents all the same.

products.name: Adjustable Thin Client Mini PC Mount, Attach to Monitor Arm and Stand
products.verdict: An open-frame metal mount that also attaches to a stand pole.
products.description:
This open-frame metal mount fits 0.63 to 2.8 inch widths and holds 12 lb. It attaches to a monitor arm, stand pole, wall or underside of a desk, and includes cable management and a pen holder. It costs under $25.

The specs nearly mirror the first-place bracket, which is why it ranks fifth. Its distinguishing points are the open frame, which lets air move around the case, and the option to clamp onto a stand pole instead of an arm. Like the leader, it lists no combined rating with the monitor.

Choose it if your monitor sits on a stand with a pole, or your PC runs warm. If the first pick already fits your setup, there is little reason to switch. Work out total load before you install anything.

products.name: Monzlteck Adjustable Small Device VESA Mount Behind the Monitor
products.verdict: A simple steel mount with a 2-screw install.
products.description:
The Monzlteck is a steel mount for devices under 2.8 inches thick, with behind-monitor, wall and under-desk options. It adds anti-scratch EVA pads, uses a 2-screw install and costs under $25.

Quick installation is the appeal, and the steel build suits a small PC. It ranks last because the listing states no weight rating, so you cannot judge how much it will carry the way you can with the 12 lb brackets. The feature set is also plain compared with the others.

Pick it for a light mini PC when you want the fastest setup. Skip it if you need a published capacity or a heavier machine. Treat it as a lightweight option and keep the PC's weight modest.

whatMatters.detail: The combined load is the monitor plus the PC, and your arm and VESA plate have limits. Exceeding them risks sagging. Add both weights and compare with the arm's rating. The HumanCentric lists 18 lb combined, so use its figure with the monitor in mind.

VESA is the hole pattern on the monitor's back, and 75x75 and 100x100mm are the common sizes. Your monitor must match the mount. Look at the back of the display or its manual, and check that the listing names the same pattern, as HumanCentric and VIVO do.

The bracket must fit your PC's thickness or depth. Listings give a range, such as 0.63 to 2.8 inches or 1.8 to 7.1 cm. Measure your case before ordering, because a PC outside the range will not seat, and the wider range of the first pick helps.

A PC behind a screen can run warm, and a closed bracket traps heat. Open frames, like the 12 lb stand-pole mount, let air move around the case. Look for open-frame in the title and leave room around the vents once it is mounted.

Simple installs save time and reduce mistakes. Check what hardware comes in the box, since some kits add wall and under-desk screws and others do not. The Monzlteck advertises a 2-screw install, while HumanCentric adds scratch strips. Read the bullets before ordering.

faq.a: It can, depending on the port layout. Check the clearance around your monitor's ports, and use a mount that leaves them accessible, before you attach the bracket.
Yes. A PC behind the screen can run warm, so favor an open frame like the stand-pole mount or the ventilated VIVO Dell model, and leave space around the vents.
Add the PC and monitor weights and compare with the arm. The HumanCentric lists an 18 lb combined rating, while the Adjustable Thin Client mount lists 12 lb for the device alone.
Only a screwdriver in most cases. The Monzlteck advertises a 2-screw install, and the other kits include their own hardware, so check the box contents on the listing.
If your arm is near its limit, yes, because it lists 18 lb combined with the monitor. If not, the cheaper Adjustable Thin Client bracket carries 12 lb for less.
Check the width range. A NUC-style box has to fall within the bracket's range, such as 0.63 to 2.8 inches on the top pick. Measure it first, since the Dell-specific VIVO will not fit other brands.

finalTake: Start with the combined weight of your monitor and PC, then pick the mount. The Adjustable Thin Client bracket suits most setups, HumanCentric makes sense when the arm is close to its limit, and VIVO gives you a 3-year warranty. Leave space around the vents, because a PC behind a screen can run warm.
